messages:
ops-bot: ALERT: elevated 429s for acct=ACME_CORP in prod-us-east-1 — 5m avg 429 rate = 17/min, threshold=5/min :rotating_light:
support_lead: FYI customer reported steady 429s since 09:03 UTC. SDK v2.3.1, multiple concurrent streams. They see `Retry-After: 60` and timeouts in their logs. Passing to eng for triage.
eng_oncall: got it. can you paste a sample response from the gateway and the route they hit? also, any recent config changes for that org?
support_lead: pasted sample from customer (redacted):
```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Retry-After: 60
X-Request-ID: req_01F23AB4
Content-Type: application/json
{"error":"rate_limit_exceeded","details":"per_minute_limit"}
```
Route: `/v1/generate` with model=redwood-xl-8k, route_id=gen-main-prod. No recent config changes on our side per billing. Customer uses 8 parallel connections from a fleet of workers.
maria_g: quick hypothesis — looks like per-minute bucket hit (RPM) not token-level. Many small concurrent requests count individually, and our gateway counts streams as separate requests. If their workers align (cron-like), minute-folding can cause spikes. can we pull a 2-minute request timestamp histogram for acct=ACME_CORP?
eng_oncall: on it. running log grep now, will post condensed counts.
eng_oncall: (paste) minute histogram UTC:
```
09:01:00 - 4 reqs
09:02:00 - 6 reqs
09:03:00 - 42 reqs
09:04:00 - 8 reqs
09:05:00 - 5 reqs
```
support_lead: that 09:03 spike aligns with customer saying "batch workers kicked off at :03" — likely synchronized jobs.
alex_w: mitigation options: 1) ask customer to jitter start times and cap concurrency (recommended long-term). 2) we can enable temporary account smoothing -> allow small burst above RPM for 1 hour. 3) increase RPM quota if agreed in contract. Which do we want to pursue now?
maria_g: short term enable smoothing + communicate client changes. Also recommend client implement exponential backoff + respect `Retry-After`. Sample backoff snippet: 
```
if (resp.status === 429) {
  const ra = parseInt(resp.headers['retry-after'] || '2', 10);
  const jitter = Math.floor(Math.random()*Math.ceil(ra*0.3));
  await sleep((ra + jitter) * 1000);
}
```
eng_oncall: I can flip smoothing for acct=ACME_CORP for 2 hours. will monitor metrics. creating temp allowance now.
ops-bot: Action logged: create_incident(INC-4521) -> "ACME_CORP 429 spike — temp smoothing enabled" assigned to eng_oncall. runbook: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/rate-limit-spike
support_lead: please also add a note to the customer steps we took and recommended client changes (jitter, lower concurrency to 2, backoff with jitter). i'll draft reply once you confirm smoothing is active.
eng_oncall: smoothing enabled at 09:18 UTC (applied policy: burst_window=30s, allowance=+25% for 2h). watching 1m/5m error rates. so far 429s dropping.
maria_g: follow-up ask for post-mitigation logs: please grab `X-RateLimit-*` headers for next 30m to verify remaining/limit usage patterns. that will help determine whether to propose quota bump.
support_lead: thanks all. i'll update the customer with the change and recommend jitter + concurrency cap. closing handoff to eng_oncall for monitoring. :white_check_mark:
